evals.prompt: Our in-house model (see app.py) writes Python dicts inside the xstructured envelope, with single quotes and True/False, so every reply fails with RecoveryError. Make xstructured accept these replies without weakening its JSON safety checks, and prove it with tests.
evals.expected_output: A JsonDecoder subclass that tries StrictJsonDecoder first, re-raises JsonSafetyError, falls back to ast.literal_eval for other ValueErrors, rejects values without a JSON form with ValueError, and is passed as decoder=. Tests subclass JsonDecoderContract and run the wrapper on the three replies with ScriptedChatModel.
assertions: A class subclasses xstructured.JsonDecoder and is passed with decoder= to with_xstructured_output
The decoder delegates to StrictJsonDecoder first and re-raises JsonSafetyError instead of falling back
Text it rejects raises ValueError (not another exception type)
A test class subclasses xstructured.testing.JsonDecoderContract and implements make_decoder
An end-to-end test parses all three replies from app.py into Decision values

evals.prompt: We want Prometheus metrics for every xstructured call in our service: calls by outcome, parse duration, and how often repair kicks in. Agents use the middleware, chat endpoints use with_xstructured_output.
evals.expected_output: An Observer subclass whose start returns a per-call Observation that records counters and a histogram in succeed and fail, counts cancellations separately, never raises, and is passed as observer= to both the wrapper and XStructuredMiddleware. Tests subclass ObserverContract.
assertions: A class subclasses xstructured.Observer and its start returns an xstructured.Observation subclass
succeed reads xstructured.parse_duration and xstructured.repaired from the attributes
fail distinguishes cancellations (asyncio.CancelledError or GeneratorExit) from errors
Metric labels use the operation and outcome, never prompt or response text
The same observer is passed with observer= to with_xstructured_output and XStructuredMiddleware

evals.prompt: Our custom RecoveryStrategy fails test_candidates_are_distinct_non_empty_substrings from xstructured's RecoveryStrategyContract. It replaces single quotes with double quotes before yielding. Fix it so the contract passes.
evals.expected_output: Explains that candidates must be substrings of the text and must never rewrite JSON, removes the quote rewriting, deduplicates and drops empty candidates, and points to a JsonDecoder subclass if non-standard quoting must be accepted.
assertions: Identifies that rewriting quotes produces candidates that are not substrings of the text
The fixed strategy yields the stripped text first and only distinct, non-empty substrings
Suggests a JsonDecoder subclass rather than a strategy for accepting non-standard syntax
Does not skip or weaken the contract test
